title: Knowledge Check 3 - Lessons 11-15
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 11-15 - Master Data Management. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: An enterprise wants a golden customer view for analytics but cannot change the CRM or ERP to consume corrected data. Which MDM style fits?
options: Centralized
Consolidation
Co-existence
Registry
questions.explanation: Consolidation builds a consolidated store for analysis without pushing data back; centralized requires consumption change (A), co-existence needs bidirectional write-back (C), and registry provides identity only without full attributes (D).

questions.question: Which TWO statements about the co-existence MDM style are TRUE?
options: The hub both consolidates data and publishes values back to sources
Data is stored only as a cross-reference, never as attributes
It supports bidirectional data flow while sources remain operational
It requires the hub to be the sole author of master data
questions.explanation: Co-existence consolidates and publishes back (A) with bidirectional flow (C); registry-style cross-reference-only describes registry (B) and sole-author describes centralized (D).

questions.question: Arrange these MDM styles from LEAST to MOST invasive to source systems.
options: Centralized, co-existence, consolidation, registry
Registry, consolidation, co-existence, centralized
Consolidation, registry, centralized, co-existence
Co-existence, registry, consolidation, centralized
questions.explanation: The spectrum runs registry (identity only) -> consolidation (read/report) -> co-existence (bidirectional) -> centralized (hub authors), so B is the correct ordering.

questions.question: Four source systems must feed two target systems. Which mapping approach minimizes effort and future change?
options: Point-to-point mapping between every source and target
A canonical model that each source maps into, and each target maps from
A single flat mapping spreadsheet per source
Direct database replication
questions.explanation: A canonical hub-and-spoke model reduces N*M point-to-point mappings to N+M and isolates change; the others scale poorly or bypass harmonization.

questions.question: Which TWO tasks belong to harmonization (before consolidation)?
options: Reconciling different code sets and date/address formats across sources
Applying survivorship rules to pick the winning attribute
Standardizing units and value domains to a canonical set
Writing the golden record back to source systems
questions.explanation: Harmonization makes values comparable (A, C) before you merge; survivorship (B) is part of consolidation and write-back (D) is a publish/co-existence step.

questions.question: A company needs both a legal entity hierarchy and a management/reporting hierarchy that differ. How should this be modeled?
options: A single self-lookup parent field
A separate hierarchy object (junction) supporting multiple hierarchy types
Two parent fields on the same record
A text field holding the hierarchy path
questions.explanation: A single parent field supports only one hierarchy, so multiple hierarchies need a hierarchy-object/junction model; text paths are unmanageable and two parent fields is not a native pattern.

questions.question: A single org receives customer records from a portal (with a stable portal ID) and from manual entry (no ID). What is the best identity-resolution approach?
options: Fuzzy matching for all records
Deterministic matching on the portal external ID for portal records, fuzzy matching for manual records
Block all manual entry
Merge every record with a similar name
questions.explanation: Use deterministic external-ID matching where a stable key exists and fuzzy matching only where it does not; fuzzy-for-all (A) is weaker, and blocking entry or name-only merging is wrong (C, D).

questions.question: Which TWO statements about Duplicate Rules are TRUE?
options: They can Block a save at the UI and/or via API
They can only warn the user, never prevent a save
They combine a matching rule with an action (Alert/Block/Allow)
They permanently merge duplicate records automatically
questions.explanation: Duplicate Rules combine matching with actions and can Alert or Block, including via API (A, C); they never auto-merge (D) and are not warn-only (B).

questions.question: A golden record is established for Account, but the telephony system is authoritative for phone numbers. What does this imply?
options: Account is not really the golden record
System of truth is attribute-level: Account masters the record, telephony masters phone
Phone must be removed from Salesforce
A second Account golden record is needed
questions.explanation: Golden records are often composite with per-attribute authoritative sources; the record can still be mastered in Salesforce while one attribute is sourced elsewhere.

questions.question: Two sources disagree on the Account phone. The ERP is ranked most trusted for billing fields but the telephony system is authoritative for phone. What determines the winning value?
options: The most recently modified value always
The attribute-level source priority / survivorship rule
The longest value
Whichever record was merged last
questions.explanation: Survivorship is attribute-level with source priority; recency (A) is only one possible rule, and length/merge-order are not rules (C, D).

questions.question: A company wants to auto-merge only highly confident duplicates and send ambiguous ones to a steward. Which configuration achieves this?
options: One threshold that auto-merges everything above 50%
Three bands: high score auto-merge, mid score manual review, low score no match
Block all saves without a tax ID
Merge only on exact name
questions.explanation: A three-band threshold design automates confident matches and routes ambiguous ones to review; single-threshold (A), block-on-ID (C), and name-only (D) are poor balances.

questions.question: Which TWO are legitimate uses of external reference data in MDM?
options: Validating and standardizing addresses
Replacing the source system as the system of record for all attributes
Enriching firmographics such as industry and company size
Determining record ownership in the CRM
questions.explanation: Reference data validates/standardizes (A) and enriches (C); it does not become the system of record for everything (B) nor set CRM ownership (D).

questions.question: For the legal name attribute, the legal/ERP system must win even if the CRM value is newer. Which survivorship approach expresses this?
options: Most recent value always wins
A composed ordered rule: legal name from ERP, else most recent validated CRM name
Longest value wins
Whichever source has more fields populated
questions.explanation: Composed ordered survivorship rules encode 'ERP wins for legal name, with fallbacks'; pure recency (A) contradicts the requirement, and length/completeness are weaker fallbacks (C, D).

questions.question: Which TWO metrics are appropriate for a data steward to monitor on the golden record?
options: Match/duplicate rate and completeness
CPU utilization of the integration server
Unresolved-conflict count and survivorship override rate
Number of page layouts on the Account object
questions.explanation: Quality metrics (A) and conflict/override counts (C) are stewardship dials; server CPU and layout counts are not data-quality measures.

questions.question: Why store provenance (winning source and timestamp) on the golden record?
options: To improve query performance
To make survivorship decisions auditable and explainable
To encrypt the attribute
To trigger record sharing
questions.explanation: Provenance makes the winner explainable and auditable; it is not a performance, encryption, or sharing feature.
